reference.title: Licensing, the GOV.UK brand and the NHS brand
reference.shortdesc: What you may reuse freely, and the identities reserved for official GOV.UK services and for NHS organisations.

section.title: The plugin
section.p: The plugin is published under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The vendored govuk-frontend assets keep their own MIT licence, including the NHS-palette recompile built from govuk-frontend's Sass. Neither licence grants any right to the GOV.UK brand or to the NHS brand.

section.title: Reserved identities
section.p: Four things are reserved — two for official GOV.UK services, two for NHS organisations — and none of them is shipped by this plugin as a file:

dlentry.dd: Permitted only on services on the gov.uk domain, delivered by or for a government department. The neutral and iStandUK themes carry no crown. In official mode the crown-and-wordmark is drawn inline from govuk-frontend's MIT-licensed artwork; the footer's crown crest image is never shipped.
Licensed for official use only. The plugin aliases it to a system font stack, so no restricted font file is ever downloaded; an entitled service adds the typeface through args.css.

The NHS letters and logo are restricted to NHS organisations; any other body needs permission from NHS England or the Department of Health and Social Care. In NHS mode the logo is drawn inline from nhsuk-frontend's MIT-licensed artwork; no other mode carries it.
The NHS brand font is licensed to NHS organisations and is not bundled; NHS mode falls back to Arial unless the publisher supplies the font.

section.note: Enabling govuk.branding=official asserts that your service is entitled to the GOV.UK brand, and govuk.branding=nhs that your organisation is entitled to the NHS identity. Both modes warn in the build log every time they are used. Only turn them on when that entitlement is real.
